name: Lumbar Facet-Mediated Pain
definition: Axial low-back pain suspected to arise from lumbar zygapophyseal joints. History, examination and imaging cannot reliably confirm the facet joint as the pain source by themselves.

typical: Pain may increase with extension/rotation or prolonged standing
Buttock or proximal-thigh referral may occur
Usually no true dermatomal neurological deficit

redFlags.item: Neurological deficit or cauda equina features
Trauma/fracture risk, systemic infection or malignancy features

investigations.principle: Imaging may identify degeneration but does not prove a painful facet origin.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI for red flags or alternative neural/structural pathology.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may show facet arthropathy but are not diagnostic of facet-mediated pain.

amber: Diagnostic medial branch blocks and radiofrequency procedures are specialist options for carefully selected persistent cases.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Possible Kati-shoola/Kati-graha symptom correlation; no one-to-one classical equivalence.

patientEducation.summary: Axial low-back pain suspected to arise from lumbar zygapophyseal joints. History, examination and imaging cannot reliably confirm the facet joint as the pain source by themselves.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
